newsitem.title: USA: Detroit Purchasing Managers July index rises.
newsitem.headline: Detroit Purchasing Managers July index rises.

text.p: The National Association of Purchasing Management-Metro Detroit's composite July index rose to 52.2 from 48.3 in June, according to a Comerica Inc survey released Monday.
An index below 50 signals a slowing manufacturing economy, while a reading above 50 suggests expansion, according to the survey of southeastern Michigan's industrial economy.
A year ago, in July 1996, the index was 52.8, or 0.6 points above current levels.
"During July, the non-automotive sector of the local economy carried the ball," said David Littmann, senior economist with Detroit-based Comerica Bank, a unit of Comerica Inc.
"Production and new order activity showed modest expansion, while employment shrunk in both automotive and non-automotive segments of the marketplace," he said.
